title: Physics 1: Mechanics
subject: Mechanics
summary: Calculus-based Newtonian mechanics, from kinematics and Newton's laws through energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, oscillations and a brief look at fluids. Builds the problem-solving habits (free-body diagrams, conservation laws, limiting-case checks) needed for every later course; chemistry hooks include potential-energy curves, reduced mass, moments of inertia and damped resonance.

units.title: Units, Estimation & Vectors
units.summary: The working toolkit for every later lesson: units, dimensional analysis, order-of-magnitude estimates and vector algebra (dot and cross products); the chemist's unit-conversion habits carry over directly.

lessons.title: Units, Dimensional Analysis & Fermi Estimates
objectives: Convert between SI and other unit systems by chaining conversion factors, and check a result's units at every step.
Use dimensional analysis to test whether a formula can be correct and to guess the form of a relation such as T ~ sqrt(l/g).
Make a Fermi estimate of an unfamiliar quantity (e.g. molecules in a breath of air) by decomposing it into factors good to a power of ten.
Report an answer with an appropriate number of significant figures and state when a result is only good to an order of magnitude.
